structure: Part 2 read the high-risk plants task-list hub and the journey flow that feeds it, in full: the hub feature folder (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, hub.fit.spec.js, controller.test.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js) and the flow folder (flow.js and flow.test.js, task-rows.js and task-rows.test.js, entry-guard.js and entry-guard.test.js, navigation.test.js, save-and-continue.test.js, section-captions/index.js with its unit test and copy.en.js/copy.cy.js/copy.test.js, fixtures/happy-path.json), plus the journey's config.js and test-support.js; shared/save-actions.njk and shared/section-caption.njk were read for context only (part 13 claims them), and paths.js and set.js were consulted only to resolve the route strings. It covers: the Overview hub served GET-only at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId}, its H1, task-list heading, Return to dashboard button, Back link, journey strip and accessibility structure; the four numbered hub groups and their captions in both locales; the five status words (Completed, Optional, In progress, Not yet started, Cannot start yet) and the tag styling of each; all seven task rows of task-rows.js (commodities, origin, arrival, destination, consignor, identificationNumbers, contact) with their titles, the pages and obligations each covers, where each link lands, which prerequisite blocks each and every status rule the unit and fit tests pin down, plus the review row the hub builds from the review flow section; the five flow sections (start, about-the-consignment, arrival-and-destination, consignment-parties, review), their pages and order and the readyForCheckYourAnswers gate on review; FLOW_ONLY_KEYS and the journey's session cookie names, template root and layout; what navigation.test.js and save-and-continue.test.js prove about the plants/wood and potato page order, sub-page exits, the missing-earlier-answer landing and its single log line; the entry guard's guarded and exempt paths, its committed-answer test, its redirect, its log line, its 404 and the leave-journey link; the INS notification-type question URL; the section caption of every captioned page and the pages deliberately left bare; the machine-draft state of the Welsh; the journey test-support seeds, in-scope question sets, picked-party copy shape and Back-link cases; and the five use cases the happy-path fixture encodes. It stops at the pages themselves (parts 3 to 11) and at notification-action-slugs.js (part 1).

claims.note: Looked in the hub controller, its unit tests, its fit spec and both copy files. The submitted and amending states are reached through the action slugs part 1 claims and the pages parts 3 to 11 claim.
